Posted April 17, 2004
Two articles with analysis by Richard Cowan

President Bush's recent press conference was remarkable in that the reporters did not simply accept as gospel whatever the War President said. This is in sharp contrast with the way the media treats John Walters, whose Drug War is almost never questioned. So, perhaps Bush should let Walters explain Iraq.
See
The Crisis in Democracy, Prohibitionism And The Police Fiasco. Why Will It Work In Iraq, If It Does Not Work In DEAland?
and
Embarrassing Questions: If It Was Wrong to Lie to Justify the War on Saddam, Why Isn't It Wrong to Lie to Justify the War on Cannabis Users? Analysis by Richard Cowan

Actually, there are some interesting parallels between the War on Terror and the War on Drugs. Bush claims that the Iraq War is essential to the War on Terror. Critics claim that it is making the terror problem worse, and the West is less secure because vast resources have been wasted in Iraq and the focus of our efforts has been misdirected away from Afghanistan. Everyone recognizes that even the US military has finite resources, but it is never acknowledged that the same is true of law enforcement everywhere.

Critics of the Drug War say that the War on Cannabis, although it is never acknowledged to have a separate existence, is a distraction from the much more serious problems with hard drugs, crimes of violence, and even terrorism.
See
More Proof That The Drug War Is Really A War On Cannabis. Plus: Sabotaging Medical Cannabis Research And Lying About It. Analysis by Richard Cowan
and
John Walters Says, Prescription Drug Abuse Is The Second Largest Illicit Drug Problem After Cannabis, Of Course! Different Measures for Success and Failure. Seeking New Victims.
and
All Power to The Incompetents: UK Cannabis Reform Delayed As Police Push for Arbitrary Power. Fail to Protect Royal Family, But Demand Control Over Cannabis. More That We Couldn't Make Up.

In fact, none of the questions that are being raised about the Iraq War are ever considered when John Walters speaks, no matter how bizarre his claims may be. He plays Comical Ali for the US media. Just as the former Iraqi propagandist was given a free ride by the Arab media, this week provided a truly spectacular example of the free ride that Walters gets from the DEAland media, hence my suggestion that Bush let him explain the Iraq War.

Thursday, CNN carried a Reuters story:
U.S. blames Canada for marijuana emergencies
From http://edition.cnn.com/2004/WORLD/americas/04/14/usa.canada.marijuana.reut/index.html
(MarijuanaNews note: I could not find any Canadian reports on the Czar's latest. The Canadians seem to have tuned him out.)
See
John Walters Testimony To The Canadian Parliament. The Public Record Or What He Would Have Said, If He Was Not Afraid of Being Asked Embarrassing Questions. The Battle for Canada.

MIAMI, Florida (Reuters) -- Canadian production of high-potency marijuana is partly to blame for a doubling of pot-related emergency room cases in the United States, the head of U.S. drug policy said Wednesday.

Reiterating U.S. criticism of a more relaxed Canadian attitude to marijuana, White House drug czar John Walters urged Ottawa to recognize the problem of hydroponically grown pot, which is grown in nutrient-rich solutions rather than soil.
(MarijuanaNews note: There is nothing unique about Canadian cannabis. The DEA says, Marijuana produced in Canada is recognized for its potency, but there is a general misconception regarding the uniqueness of this marijuana.Growers in both Canada and the United States have access to the same strains of cannabis seeds and the same cultivation technologies. Therefore, growers in both countries are capable of producing the same quality of high-grade marijuana.)
From http://www.usdoj.gov/ndic/pubs07/794/794p.pdf

It is often grown inside under lights, and Walters said it sold for as much as cocaine.
(MarijuanaNews note: The DEA says, reports of the reputed exchange of Canadian marijuana for U.S.cocaine on a pound-for-pound ratio are false.)
From the same source as above
http://www.usdoj.gov/ndic/pubs07/794/794p.pdf
 " Canada is exporting to us the crack of marijuana and it is a dangerous problem, " Walters told reporters in Miami, where he kicked off a campaign to cut marijuana use by Hispanic youths.
(MarijuanaNews note: The fact that he went to Miami to make this claim is even more bizarre. Does anyone really believe that Hispanic youths in Florida are smoking BC Bud?)

 " We need to have political leadership in Canada that recognizes the problem, " he said. " Addiction is going to spread in Canada dramatically. It has in many places. "
(MarijuanaNews note: The facts show otherwise. In 2003, a survey of more than 30,500 BC students in Grades 7 to 12 found that between 1998 and 2003 marijuana use had declined from 40% to 37%.

In February the Partnership crowed that over the past five years first time marijuana use declined from 42 to 39 percent. However, in BC during the same 5-year period there was a decline in the use of all illegal drugs, and legal drugs as well.)

A longtime critic of Canadian plans to decriminalize the possession of small amounts of marijuana, Walters said that while the pot the hippie generation knew contained on average 1 percent of psychoactive Delta-9-Tetrahydrocannabinol, or THC, Canada's high-potency marijuana contained 20 to 30 percent THC.
See
Dan Forbes Documents Walters Lies About Potency. Understanding That The War On Cannabis Is Built On Lies Is Key to Understanding More Than Just Drug War.
(MarijuanaNews note: Although the potency claims are bogus, one need not be an expert on cannabis or statistics to recognize that Walters compared a supposed average from the hippie generation with an extreme from today. Even such a blatant error goes unchallenged.)

" It is extremely dangerous. It is one of the reasons why we believe ... we have seen a doubling of emergency room cases involving marijuana in the last several years from 60,000 to 120,000, " Walters said.
See
Cannabis Prohibition Prostitutes Science In New Emergency Dept. Data. Hiding the Truth Behind A Cloud of Lies.
(MarijuanaNews note: Involving marijuana? The data in question is based on mentions of up to six substances by a visitor to an emergency department. Alcohol is included in this data only when it is in combination with an illegal drug, nonetheless alcohol in combination mentions totaled over 207,000.

There were over 113,000 mentions of marijuana in 2002, but only 32,000 were marijuana-only mentions, and even then marijuana was not necessarily the cause of the visit. To put this into context, there were over 100 million emergency room visits in 2002. Benzodiazepines tranquilizers like Valium accounted for over 105,000 mentions,
From http://dawninfo.samhsa.gov/pubs_94_02/pickatable/2002/2.2.0.xls

But cases involving alcohol totaled over 25 million!
See National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism.

Although blaming Canada is a new wrinkle, Walters is not the first official to use this line.)
From 1997 see
Shalala Uses ER Stats to Lie About Marijuana --Again -- as " Drug-related " ER Visits Decline

Disagreements over drug policy, combined with differences over the Iraq war, are among several issues that have chilled relations between Canada and its powerful southern neighbor.

While maintaining that improving ties with Washington was a priority, new Canadian Prime Minister Paul Martin said in December he intended to press ahead with plans to end jail terms for people caught with small amounts of marijuana.
(MarijuanaNews note: Over 100 million Americans live in decrim states.)
See
NORML Reports Marijuana Arrests For 2002 Near Record High Pot Smokers Arrested In America At A Rate Of One Every 45 Seconds Plus Analysis by Richard Cowan.
and
Jamaican Attorney General Wants Debate On Implementing Decriminalization So Does The Canadian Justice Minister. Why Isn't There An International Debate? Analysis by Richard Cowan
and
As Canada Moves Toward Some Form Of Decriminalization, Canadian Narks and Walters Escalate Lying. The New Math. Canada Replaces Mexico As Leading Supplier of Cannabis. And If You Believe That

And Ottawa has said that Washington's own data shows that of all the illegal pot seized by U.S. agents only 1.5 percent came from Canada.
(MarijuanaNews note: Oops! They did wait until the end of the article to insert a factoid that contradicts the premise of the story, but this could be a dangerous precedent.)

The head of the White House Office of National Drug Policy said that Canadian producers had a multibillion dollar marijuana growing business and that 80 to 90 percent of revenues came from the United States.

He said Toronto authorities told him there were up to 15,000 indoor growers in that metropolitan area alone.

(MarijuanaNews note: Agence France Press also carried this story, with a few more twists.)

Canada is a major exporter of high-potency marijuana to the US: drug czar

MIAMI (AFP) - Canada is a major exporter of high-grade marijuana to the United States, US drug czar John Walters said in Miami, suggesting Canadian authorities were too lax in punishing drug traffickers.

" We have a growing problem with the expansion of particularly high-potency marijuana coming from Canada, " said Walters, who heads the White House Office of National Drug Control Policy.

" The growth of high-potency marijuana has exploded in Canada, " he said at a news conference.

He said new cultivation methods mean the marijuana sold in the United States today is on average seven times more potent " than the marijuana baby-boomer parents may remember from their days of use or experimentation. "

In the past, marijuana contained about one percent tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), the drug's active ingredient. " The indoor-cultivated hydroponic, specially tended marijuana can go up to 20 to 30 percent THC content, " Walters said.

" Canada is exporting to us the crack of marijuana, " he said.

He said high-potency marijuana sold for about the same price per weight as cocaine, and that some motorcycle gangs in California swapped the marijuana they brought from the United States' northern neighbor for the same weight of cocaine.
(MarijuanaNews note: The DEA and the RCMP disagree: RCMPinvestigations also indicate that traffickers occasionally exchange high-potency marijuana for cocaine at a ratio of about three units of marijuana to one of cocaine.) emphasis added.
From http://www.usdoj.gov/dea/pubs/intel/01001-intellbrief.pdf

This is an old version of the party line, from 1998 see
New Party Line In Prohibitionist Propaganda For DEAland/Canada Border
(Disguised As Journalism In Vancouver

Last year, authorities estimated marijuana trafficking was a nine-billion-dollar business in British Columbia alone, said Walters.
See
Voice of America Becomes Latest Organization to Be Corrupted By Cannabis Prohibition. Canadian Collaborators Lie To Undermine Their Country's Freedom and Sovereignty. The Myth of BC Bud.
 (MarijuanaNews note: If the Canadian cannabis crop is a big as the prohibitionists claim, and if 80 to 90 percent of it really does go to the States, and if Canada provides only 1.5 of imports (based on actual seizures, the only hard number in this scenario), then the US marijuana market is vastly bigger than even the Feds want to admit.)

" The real problem in Canada has been that ... the judges have refused in a large measure to give people jail time unless they actually commit a violent crime. As a result you can make millions of dollars distributing drugs which cause all kinds of damages to lives and not go to jail, " he said.
See
Prohibition and The Prison State. Protecting Youth and Minorities. In DEAland, The UK and France Prisons Are Full.
